author: Otto Jevne and Peter M. Almini, publishers; Chicago Lithographing Co., lithographers; text by James W. Sheahan
repository: University of Michigan copy, digitised by HathiTrust (mdp.69015000002622). The Chamber of Commerce plate (PDF page 8 of the copy read) is committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3688/chicago_illustrated_chamber_of_commerce_plate.jpg.
locator: Plate 'Chamber of Commerce' (PDF page 8) and its letterpress (PDF pages 9-10), which places it at the south-east corner of LaSalle and Washington streets fronting the Court-House square and gives it as 93 by 181 feet, 100 feet high, E. Burling architect, a Mansard roof, dedicated 30 August 1865, cost about $400,000.
rights_note: Published 1866-1867 in the United States; public domain (HathiTrust: Public Domain).
access_notes: Read 2026-11-19 (T-3688) from page images of the HathiTrust copy already committed at chicago/pre_fire_v1/media/research/illustrated-pdfpage8.png, -9.png and -10.png; the plate re-saved as JPEG for the image gate, sha256 9e1a7af19fbb354ea25fe844364c669115642dfde5085e2dc2df238cde1a4eaa.
note: A tinted lithograph drawn from a viewpoint on Washington Street north-west of the building, a little more frontal than Carbutt's photograph; it agrees with the photograph on the bays, the entrance arcade, the windows and the mansard, and adds the clock in the scrolled centre pediment and a flagstaff over it. Its letterpress gives the dimensions and the architect. A drawing, so it is read for elements and checked against the photograph for proportion.
what_it_supplies: the Chamber of Commerce's place, size, height, architect, date and cost
